steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Social class and achievement: working-class students consistently achieve less well than middle-class students. External factors: material deprivation (poorer housing, less study space, no internet), cultural deprivation (Bernstein: restricted code vs elaborated code), cultural capital (Bourdieu: middle-class knowledge, tastes and values give advantage in school). Internal factors: streaming and labelling (Becker: teachers have an 'ideal pupil' image that is middle-class). | Key Fact: Gender and achievement: girls now outperform boys at every level (61% of girls vs 50% of boys achieve 5+ GCSEs A*-C). Reasons for girls' improvement: feminism (changed aspirations), changing family patterns (more women-headed households), employment opportunities (more jobs for women), GCSE coursewo

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how social class affects educational achievement, using external and internal factors. | Evaluate why girls now outperform boys in education. | Assess the relative importance of external and internal factors in creating ethnic differences in educational achievement.
